points chart, the prize table, the Annex J lane grid, the Annex G/H checklists.

merged into the index as normal searchable rules.

records.title: Course re-entry diagram (5-minute countdown)
records.note: Diagram printed in the rulebook, p. 8 — described here.
records.text:
Diagram illustrating article 4.11 / 4.11.1.

The course is drawn as four quadrants: the back stretch is split into two halves and the front stretch into two halves, divided at the mid-course buoy and at the centre line.

The diagram is labelled, in French and English:
- "Bateau immobilisé / Boat dead in the water"
- "L'embarcation doit réintégrer le parcours là où elle est entrée. / The boat must re-enter the course at the same place where it entered."

Dashed arrows show boats leaving the racecourse and looping back in at the same point they exited — a boat that stops in the middle of the course during the countdown must re-enter where it entered, and boats already on the racecourse have priority over boats re-entering.

records.title: 2026 HRL Capsule Training Evaluation Chart
records.note: Printed as an image in the annexes — transcribed here. This is the sheet an official fills in during the capsule test (mandatory every two years, see rule 13.8).
records.text:
2026 HRL Capsule Training Evaluation Chart — each line is marked Pass / Fail / N/A.

STEP 1 — Physical and visual verifications of the driver's equipment
- Racing suit: HRL logo positioned on the upper front right side; handles on shoulders
- Shoes / gloves: shoes; gloves
- Helmet (max 12 years, refer to UIM list of authorized helmets): manufacturer; serial number; model; homologation; date of manufacture; 50% or more must contain one or more highly visible colour
- Mask: brand and type; any defect or damage; in visual working order
- Air system: hose and T-connector in good working order; hoses are fluorescent yellow; hoses are secured to the helmet
- Head and neck restraint system: brand and date of manufacture; certified SFI 38.1 or FIA 8858-2002 / 8858-2010
- Life jacket: brand and date of manufacture; category (capsule jacket / capsule suit / racing uniform)

STEP 2 — Underwater breathing and equipment test
- Mask is properly adjusted to the face of the driver (no leak)
- The driver is comfortable breathing underwater for a minimum of 2 minutes
- Hose is in working order (no air leak)
- The driver is comfortable during the process of switching air supply
- The driver is able to remove, replace and purge his equipment underwater
- The driver is able to remove his mask, receive a regulator from the diver and breathe

STEP 3 — Immersion test (scored separately for small capsule and big capsule)
- The driver is comfortably installed in the cockpit
- The driver did a verification of the air supply
- The driver familiarizes with the capsule safety equipment
- The driver demonstrates his ability to release steering wheel, harness and canopy
- The driver reviewed the extrication procedures (6 mandatory steps)
- The driver shows a thumbs up that he is ready to flip
- The driver waited until the capsule is filled with water and the diver signs to begin
- The driver unhooked and opened the canopy
- The driver took off the steering wheel
- The driver undid the arm pin and removed the arm
- The driver undid the safety harness
- The driver extricated himself from the cockpit to the side
- The driver informed the rescue team with a clasp of hands above head as an "okay" signal

records.title: Safety inspection checklist
records.note: Printed as an image in the annexes — transcribed here. The leading digit is the compliance deadline: 1 = mandatory to race, no exception · 2 = mandatory for the next race · 3 = mandatory for the next racing weekend · 4 = mandatory for the next season. Every line is marked Pass / Fail / N/A.
records.text:
HRL safety inspection checklist (Annex H). Leading digit = deadline: 1 mandatory to race · 2 next race · 3 next racing weekend · 4 next season.

HELMET (rating no greater than 12 years from SNELL date) — brand, type
1 DOT · 1 Snell number · 1 Head and neck restraint system certified SFI 38.1 or FIA 8858-2002 / 8858-2010 (brand, fabrication date, recertification date)

DRIVER'S SUIT
1 Handles on shoulders · 1 SFI certified · 4 Material (polyester)

RESTRAINT BELT
1 5 points / type (latch or rotary) · 1 SFI certified · 4 Belt bolt attach (grade 8) · 3 Expiry date must be followed

AIR SYSTEM — mask brand
4 Air bottle 13 ft³ (ambient air) · 4 Air bottle 30 ft³ (permanent air) · 1 Air hose between 10 and 15 feet long · 1 Leg holster system (6 ft³) · 4 Air tank holder in centre section of the boat

LIFE JACKET
1 Brand · 1 Category (capsule jacket / capsule suit / racing uniform)

HULL
3 Critical information on bottom hull · 3 Trailer identified with boat number in front · 1 Fire extinguisher 5 lbs (min 3A40BC, in service date) with boat number · 3 Strut accessible for viewing · 4 RH rollover bracket (min 3/4 hole) · 1 Sling attachments accessible for viewing · 3 Cowling flotation (must float by itself) · 1 Mirrors · 1 External release or hand hold opening for cockpit lid · 3 Backwater valve / check valve · 3 Front towing hook · 3 Front wing bushings · 1 Propeller cover made of cut-resistant fabric or a protective guard/cage · 3 Skid fin and mounting bracket accessible for viewing · 4 Inside cockpit white (2024 build and newer)

ENGINE
1 Cockpit area sealed from engine bay · 1 Auxiliary throttle return spring, 2, no idle screw (gas pedal is optional) · 3 Engine mounts · 3 Battery mounts · 1 Fuel tank / fuel pick-up must be accessible for viewing · 1 Gas tank vent · 1 Fuel lines · 3 Oil / water lines · 1 Prop shaft collars, 2 (screw or split)

STEERING
1 Integrity of components and attachments · 1 Steering wheel and rudder properly coordinated / turnbuckles double wrap

COCKPIT PADDING
3 Minimum 2" behind driver's head · 3 Energy absorbing foam in cockpit

COCKPIT / CANOPY
4 Min 2" clearance above driver / rider to cockpit / canopy · 4 No wing pedal activation rods permitted to pass through the capsule · 3 No sharp edges in cockpit · 1 Accuclock · 4 Air hold / entry and exit · 1 Canopies must have internal release and handhold · 1 Lanyard on seat belt latch bright yellow · 3 Release pin on steering column bright yellow · 1 Escape hatch opens and closes easily · 3 Capsule lid hinge and latch bright yellow
